deepDives.title: Weak peso expected to factor into DBCC outlook
deepDives.summary: THE Department of Budget and Management (DBM) said the weakness of the peso is expected to influence the…
reasons: reader relevance 2/3: DBM says peso weakness will shape budget outlook
promoted to deep dive in place of "Another fuel price rollback expected next week"

article.text:
THE Department of Budget and Management (DBM) said the weakness of the peso is expected to influence the Development Budget Coordination Committee (DBCC) views on the economy when it delivers its year-end briefing next month.
“All of those economic indicators that we see right now will be laid on the table,” Budget Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon told reporters on the sidelines of ASEAN Business Investment Summit.
“We don’t want to preempt, of course, the meeting because that is where the decision will be made,” he added.
“Lahat naman ng macro-indicators tinitignan ’yon (All macro-indicators will be looked at), both domestic and international, because they shape how the economy will move and grow,” he said.
He added that the DBCC closely monitors movements in the exchange rate. The DBCC projects the peso-dollar rate to average P60-P62 this year.
The peso breached the P64-per-dollar level on Oct. 27, hitting a new record low of P64.17.
On Friday, the peso closed at P63.72 against the greenback, weakening by 2 centavos from its P63.7 close on Nov. 12.
The DBCC is expected to meet in the third week of December for its year-end review of the government’s macroeconomic assumptions.
The economy grew by just 2.1% year on year in the July-to-September period, slowing from 4% in the same period last year and the revised 2.4% in the second quarter.
The third-quarter performance brought GDP growth in the first nine months to 2.5%, well below the government’s 3.5%-4.5% full-year target.
Economy Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan has said that the economy would have to grow by about 6.3% in the fourth quarter to achieve the lower end of the government’s full-year target. — Justine Irish D. Tabile

article.text:
Seventy overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) from Saudi Arabia have been repatriated to the Philippines amid continuing tensions in the Middle East, the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) said Saturday.
The repatriated OFWs arrived at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) Terminal 3 on November 13, 2026, according to a Facebook post by the DMW.
To date, the agency reported that up to 1,170 OFWs and their dependents have already been brought home to the Philippines in coordination with the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA).
They also received assistance through the government's Unified Package for Livelihoods, Industry, Food, and Transport (UPLIFT) Program for Filipino households affected by the Middle East conflict.

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines is exploring access to emergency oil stocks in Indonesia and Thailand to bolster its energy security as the months-long Middle East war continues to disrupt global fuel supplies.
State-run PNOC Exploration Corp. has signed separate letters of intent (LOIs) with Indonesia’s PT Interport Mandiri Utama and The Shell Co. of Thailand Ltd. to explore possible cooperation on oil ticketing mechanisms.
Also signatories to the LOIs were the Economic Research Institute for ASEAN and East Asia (ERIA) and the Indonesian Business Council, which will serve as knowledge partners for the parties.
The preliminary agreements will facilitate pilot projects to explore the use of existing oil storage facilities in Indonesia and Thailand to give the Philippines access to petroleum reserves during supply disruptions.
Under an oil-ticketing arrangement, a participating entity pays for the right to access oil stored in another country during an emergency, subject to agreed conditions.
This could offer the Philippines an alternative to establishing new storage facilities and procuring additional oil stocks upfront.
The proposed pilot projects were announced over the weekend at the ASEAN Business and Investment Summit in Manila.
This initiative comes as the Philippines works to build its own government-maintained oil reserves, with PNOC targeting the completion of the first storage tank by end-2027.
Critics have raised concerns, however, over the high costs of building and maintaining domestic reserves, warning that these expenses could eventually be passed on to consumers.
Alongside efforts to build its own emergency reserves, the Philippines has also pushed for regional cooperation on joint oil stockpiling amid growing energy security concerns.
In its study on the ASEAN oil stockpiling strategy, ERIA examines how countries can combine national reserves, oil-ticketing arrangements and joint stockpiling.
It also outlines a phased approach to putting the strategy in place.
The study found that the region could save about $610 million annually in oil stockholding costs by increasing the volume of joint reserves from 10 to 30 days while maintaining the same overall stock levels.
“Most ASEAN member states have relatively limited emergency oil stocks, highlighting the need for stronger preparedness and regional cooperation,” ERIA said.

related.title: Banks set branch schedules for 3-day Asean Summit holiday

reasons: reader relevance 2/3: Bank branch hours during Nov 18 NCR holiday

article.text:
BANKS have announced their branch schedules in Metro Manila starting today up to Nov. 18, which was earlier declared a special non-working holiday for the National Capital Region (NCR) as the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) Summit happens.
The Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI) said all its branches across Metro Manila would remain open during the three-day period, although operations may be adjusted due to road closures, traffic restrictions and security measures related to the summit.
UnionBank of the Philippines will keep 12 Metro Manila branches open from Nov. 16 to 18, while temporarily closing its other branches in the capital region. Its branches outside Metro Manila will remain operational.
The UnionBank branches that will remain open are Glorietta, BGC Uptown Place Mall, Dasmariñas-Binondo, Wackwack, Eastwood City, Kalookan, Las Piñas-Pamplona, Alabang Town Center, Medical Center Parañaque, UnionBank Plaza, St. Francis Shangri-La Place and South Triangle.
Metrobank, meanwhile, will close 14 Metro Manila branches during the three-day holiday. Customers may transact at nearby branches identified in its branch schedule.
The affected branches include Aseana-Midpark Howell Tower, Metropolitan Park-Roxas Boulevard, Metropolitan Park-iMET, JP Laurel-San Miguel Manila, Adriatico, Ocean Tower, Anda Circle-Port Area, Intramuros, Intramuros-CBCP, Ermita, Luneta-T.M. Kalaw, Robinson’s Place-Adriatico, Roxas Boulevard-Padre Faura, and Roxas Boulevard-Vito Cruz.
Metrobank said its automated teller machines (ATMs), cash acceptance machines (CAMs), and withdrawal and deposit machines (WDMs) would remain available. Customers may also use Metrobank Online and its mobile application.
BDO Unibank announced that selected branches would remain open during the holiday. Its published list of open branches covers branches across Metro Manila. Customers may also use BDO Online, BDO Pay and its ATMs and Universal Teller Machines.
Philippine National Bank (PNB) released a holiday banking schedule, listing selected branches that will operate from 9 a.m. to noon during the holiday. Its advisory includes 50 branches scheduled to open on Nov. 16 and another 50 on Nov. 17.
Security Bank also listed selected branches that will operate during the holiday, with schedules varying by day. Customers may check the bank’s banking advisory for the complete list.
Asia United Bank (AUB) said 28 selected branches in the National Capital Region would remain open from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. during the holiday. All other NCR branches will be closed and resume regular operations on Nov. 19, while provincial branches will operate from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
Rizal Commercial Banking Corp. (RCBC) will also keep selected Metro Manila branches open during the three-day period, with operating hours following their regular schedules. The bank published separate lists of open branches for Nov. 16, 17 and 18. Branches outside Metro Manila will maintain their regular schedules.
Bank of Commerce said selected branches would remain open during the holiday, with 15 branch entries listed for each day from Nov. 16 to 18. The operating branches vary daily.
The three-day special non-working holiday was declared under Proclamation 1447 to ease traffic congestion and allow authorities to ensure the safety and security of participants in the Asean Summit and related meetings.
Customers are advised to check their respective banks’ official channels for branch schedules and possible changes in operations. They may also use available digital banking platforms and automated teller machines for transactions during the holiday.

reasons: reader relevance 2/3: Stocks face stagflation downside risk this week

article.text:
PHILIPPINE equities could face further downside this week as slowing economic growth, elevated inflation and expectations of additional interest rate hikes keep investors cautious, with the benchmark index already falling to its lowest closing level in nearly a year.
The Philippine Stock Exchange index (PSEi) ended last week at 5,593.49, down 168.46 points, or 2.92 percent, reversing the previous week’s 1.4-percent gain. The index also fell below the 5,600 level on Friday, reflecting continued weakness in investor sentiment.
The PSEi fell for three consecutive trading sessions and was lower in five of the last six sessions, closing near its lowest level since October 2026 and marking its weakest closing level in almost a year.
Foreign investors were also net sellers, recording outflows of $4.7 million for the week, a reversal from the $28.1 million in net buying recorded during the previous holiday-shortened trading week.
The worsening economic outlook has reinforced concerns about stagflation, as the economy struggles with slower growth alongside persistent price pressures.
Michael Ricafort, chief economist at Rizal Commercial Banking Corp., said the market’s decline reflected concerns over weaker domestic economic conditions, higher inflation and uncertainties surrounding the global financial environment.
